issue_title: [Bug]:   SUCCESS is set before LL_LPUART_SetBaudRate executes and before BRR validation — function can return SUCCESS with an invalid BRR
clean_text:
Title: [Bug]:   SUCCESS is set before LL_LPUART_SetBaudRate executes and before BRR validation — function can return SUCCESS with an invalid BRR

Body:
### Bug Summary

bad code

### Detailed Description

  File: stm32g0xx_ll_lpuart.c (and stm32g0xx_ll_usart.c — same pattern)
	•  Issue 1: status = SUCCESS is set before LL_LPUART_SetBaudRate executes and before BRR validation — function can return SUCCESS with an invalid BRR
	•  Issue 2: BRR range checks use assert_param which is a no-op without USE_FULL_ASSERT, so there is no runtime validation in production builds
	•  Issue 3: On the error path (bad clock/baudrate), CR1/CR2/CR3/PRESC are already written, leaving the peripheral half-configured

### Expected Behavior

_No response_

### Actual Behavior

_No response_

### Environment

_No response_

### Severity

Normal

Comments:
[KRASTM - 2026-05-20T14:51:13Z]
Hello @egtduncanbarclay,

Thank you for the report.

Regarding the issues, the status variable in **LL_LPUART_Init()** is not intended to validate the BRR. Its role is simply to indicate whether LL_LPUART_Init() was able to initialize the LPUART registers according to the parameters provided in **LPUART_InitTypeDef**.

Also, **LL_LPUART_SetBaudRate()** is implemented as a **__STATIC_INLINE** function. By design, it is used to perform small register-level operations efficiently with minimal call overhead. If you need BRR checking, you should enable USE_FULL_ASSERT and implement your own assert_failed() handler so that any invalid parameter can be handled in a way that matches your application requirements.

This is consistent with the LL approach, which prioritizes lightweight direct register access and minimal overhead. In comparison, the HAL layer provides more built-in checks and a higher level of abstraction.

With regards,

[KRASTM - 2026-05-26T09:35:05Z]
Hello @egtduncanbarclay,

Please allow me to close the issue. Thank you for your understanding.

With regards,

Title: [Question]: HAL_TIM_PWM_Stop stops complete htim instance

Body:
### Question Summary

Why does HAL_TIM_PWM_Stop stop the complete timer peripheral

### Detailed Description

In the HAL_TIM_PWM_Stop in the file stm32g0xx_hal_tim.c (version 1.6.3) the Macro__HAL_TIM_DISABLE(htim); is called. This is a bit confusing, since I would expect only the specific Channel from the functions arguments to be disabled. 
Is this the intended behaviour?

Comments:
[ASAHSTM - 2026-04-16T16:28:34Z]
Hello @JRStolle,

Thank you for your report,

This behavior is intentional. HAL_TIM_PWM_Stop first disables only the requested PWM channel, then calls __HAL_TIM_DISABLE.
However, __HAL_TIM_DISABLE disables the timer counter only if all CCx/CCxN channels are already disabled.

Therefore:
- If other channels on the same timer are still active, the timer keeps running.
- If you stop the last active channel, the timer is stopped.

With Regards,

[JRStolle - 2026-04-17T05:44:25Z]
Thank you for your reply.
Yes, I did not look inside the Makro, since the description said that it disables the TIM peripheral. 
So if I want to disable the peripheral I have to make sure, to disable all channels first. 
This might be good idea to put into the description.
Thanks!

issue_title: LL_TIM_ClearFlag_UPDATE() does not respect the reserved bits
clean_text:
Title: LL_TIM_ClearFlag_UPDATE() does not respect the reserved bits

Body:
All TIMx status registers documented in RM0444 have some bits which state "Reserved, must be kept at reset value".

You then normally read the register, modify the bits you are interested in, and then write the new value. Usually, this is done with MODIFY_REG.

This is done for compatibility reasons, in case some newer microcontroller has more flags at the reserved bits.

However, LL_TIM_ClearFlag_UPDATE() overwrites all bits.

I would at least write a comment in LL_TIM_ClearFlag_UPDATE() stating whether that could be a problem.

Comments:
[KRASTM - 2025-07-30T16:18:57Z]
Hello again @rdiez,

Regarding this issue, LL_TIM_ClearFlag_UPDATE() does not overwrite all bits. If you look at any TIMx_SR register in the RM0444, you will see the abbreviation rc_w0 (see page 55 of the RM0444):
**read/clear write0 (rc_w0) Software can read as well as clear this bit by writing 0. Writing 1 has no effect on the bit value**

Since writing 1 has no effect. That's why we have WRITE_REG(TIMx->SR, ~(TIM_SR_UIF)); inside LL_TIM_ClearFlag_UPDATE()

With regards,
Karim

[rdiez - 2025-07-31T07:10:00Z]
In understand now, thanks.

But shouldn't the reserved bits be documented as "rc_w0" then?

At the moment, the documentation only states "Reserved, must be kept at reset value". Given that the reset value is documented as 0, but writing a 0 would clear the bit, then the documentation is misleading, isn't it? It should actually say that all reserved bits should be written with 1.

[KRASTM - 2025-08-06T13:43:14Z]
Hello @rdiez,

I have checked with our team, and it seems that for the sake of code flexibility (given the wide variety of timers), the Clear functions for the LL bits are always implemented in the same way, given that the reserved bits are neither significant nor impacted. It was a decision made by our development team.

Thank you for your understanding, please allow me to close the issue.

With regards,

[rdiez - 2025-08-06T13:50:03Z]
Like I said, this is rather a documentation issue. The way it is written at the moment, it makes you scratch your head.

I am guessing that you want to close this bug because this area is only about the library, and not about the documentation. Closing this bug is OK then.

Is there a way to raise a separate bug against the documentation?

[KRASTM - 2025-08-06T14:17:59Z]
Hi,

I understand what you are trying to say, and I know you meant the documentation. That's why I checked with our team. I tried to explain the circumstances and the decision that was made by our team. We are not trying to close the issue, but there is no plan in this case.

Thank you.

With regards,

[rdiez - 2025-08-06T15:00:03Z]
I do not quite understand your answer. I gather that there is no way to raise a separate bug for the documentation, or that you are not willing to fix the documentation. Is that correct?

[KRASTM - 2025-08-06T15:09:33Z]
Hello @rdiez,

As I said, unfortunately there is no plan to fix it.

With regards,

issue_title: HAL_TIM_OnePulse_ConfigChannel and other OnePulse functions only support i/o channels 1 and 2
clean_text:
Title: HAL_TIM_OnePulse_ConfigChannel and other OnePulse functions only support i/o channels 1 and 2

Body:
**Caution**
The Issues are strictly limited for the reporting of problem encountered with the software provided in this project.
For any other problem related to the STM32 product, the performance, the hardware characteristics and boards, the tools the environment in general, please post a topic in the [ST Community/STM32 MCUs forum](https://community.st.com/s/group/0F90X000000AXsASAW/stm32-mcus) 

**Describe the set-up**
 * The board (either ST RPN reference or your custom board): STM32G0B1
 * IDE or at least the compiler and its version: Keil uVision 5.39

**Describe the bug**
The OnePulse functions in stm32g0xx_hal_tim.c support only channels 1 and 2 even though the HW supports input/output from channels 3 and 4 on any timers that have these channels. When configuring the timer in PWM mode for example, the functions seem to accept any channel from 1 to 6.

**How To Reproduce**
Call function HAL_TIM_OnePulse_ConfigChannel with any channel other than channel 1 or 2 as its input/output


**Additional context**
I have reimplemented HAL_TIM_OnePulse_Init, HAL_TIM_OnePulse_Start and HAL_TIM_OnePulse_ConfigChannel so that they will support getting the input from channel 1 or 2 but getting the output to channel 4. I have also tested this on an actual MCU with TIM1 and the timer worked as expected. I honestly do not understand why this was implemented this way in the first place if there is no HW limitation.

I have forwarded the issue to our team, and they agree that there is nothing to prevent the use of other timer channels. Unfortunately, however, there are no plans to fix this problem. Thankfully, you have managed to implement and use the other channels.

issue_title: HAL_GPIO_EXTI_Callback missing from STM32G0 HAL GPIO API
clean_text:
Title: HAL_GPIO_EXTI_Callback missing from STM32G0 HAL GPIO API

Body:
Ali Labbene requested that I open a new issue here in this thread:
https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeG0/issues/7#issuecomment-2491193412

The STM32G0 HAL library does not include the standard HAL GPIO external interrupt callback. This is what we would expect:

void HAL_GPIO_EXTI_Callback(uint16_t GPIO_Pin)
{
}

Instead, STM32G0 only includes HAL_GPIO_EXTI_Rising_Callback() and HAL_GPIO_EXTI_Falling_Callback(). These functions are fine, but HAL_GPIO_EXTI_Callback is the standard API that is used with most (if not all) other STM32 HAL drivers, and if you google any "how to make an stm32 respond to GPIO" tutorial / walk through, HAL_GPIO_EXTI_Callback is the method that is shown.

How To Reproduce:

Compare stm32g0xx_hal_gpio.h in this repository to to https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32f4xx-hal-driver/blob/master/Inc/stm32f4xx_hal_gpio.h and you will see the API method in question is missing in STM32G0.

Comments:
[TOUNSTM - 2024-12-18T14:06:24Z]
Hello @insolace,

Thank you for your contribution. This change is actually a new feature that enhances the functionality of the STM32G0 HAL library. By distinguishing between rising and falling edge interrupts.
To implement this new feature, it was necessary to break compatibility with the previous single callback method. The reason for this is that there is a single entry point for the HAL GPIO interrupt service routine: HAL_GPIO_EXTI_IRQHandler(). It is not feasible to support both the legacy single callback method and the new dual callback method within this single entry point.

As a result, you will need to adapt your code to align with the new implementation. By doing so, you will be able to take full advantage of the new hardware capabilities.

Thank you for your understanding and cooperation.
Best Regards,

issue_title: HAL I2C produces unwanted NACKs in slave mode
HAL_SPI_TransmitReceive_IT crashes when TX buffer is not 16 bit aligned
clean_text:
Title: HAL_SPI_TransmitReceive_IT crashes when TX buffer is not 16 bit aligned

Body:
**Describe the set-up**
 * Tested on nucleo-g0b1re
 * arm-none-eabi-gcc version 10.3.1 (but compiler does not matter)

**Describe the bug**
Calling function HAL_SPI_Receive_IT() or HAL_SPI_TransmitReceive_IT() with buffer not aligned to 16 bits crashes MCU

**How To Reproduce**
1. Call HAL_SPI_Receive_IT() with unaligned buffer and more then 1 byte to send

**Additional context**
Real problem however is in SPI_2linesTxISR_8BIT() function that tries to optimize send using 16 bits access if there is more data.
For **Cortex-M0+** unaligned read results in fault.

c
static void SPI_2linesTxISR_8BIT(struct __SPI_HandleTypeDef *hspi)
{
  /* Transmit data in packing Bit mode */
  if (hspi->TxXferCount >= 2U &&
    ((uint32_t)(hspi->pTxBuffPtr) & 1) == 0) // <= !!!! Additional check to use 8 bit for unaligned buffer here fixes the problem
  {
    hspi->Instance->DR = *((uint16_t *)hspi->pTxBuffPtr); // <= !!! Crashes here on Cortex-M0+
    hspi->pTxBuffPtr += sizeof(uint16_t);
    hspi->TxXferCount -= 2U;
  }
...

Comments:
[KRASTM - 2024-06-19T09:43:51Z]
ST internal Reference: 184492

[KRASTM - 2024-08-15T09:54:46Z]
Fixed in commit https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32g0xx_hal_driver/commit/1c95709a51b5a32e02c1469e12e5cfe6b8a1ce71

[kasjer - 2024-08-15T10:31:50Z]
It's hard do believe that simple bug (unnecessary optimization that was flawed and could be fixed in one line) resulted in change of API that is less functional than before, adds a lot of checks that are not really needed.
It's not that SPI hardware has some limitation that restrict buffer alignment it's just unreasonable approach that uses "optimization".
Now if one uses DMA API that works fine and for some reason wants to switch to IT that has similar API and could be used interchangeable user can face serious crash and go through debugging to find out that both API are not compatible and application has to be aware of this unnecessary limitation (that is not present in non-Cortex-M0 based MCU's).

This is very disappointing solution and hardly could be referred as fixed but if counts toward KPI.

issue_title: Timeout parameter in HAL_I2C_Master_Receive/HAL_I2C_Mem_Read not used for I2C_WaitOnFlagUntilTimeout function
clean_text:
Title: Timeout parameter in HAL_I2C_Master_Receive/HAL_I2C_Mem_Read not used for I2C_WaitOnFlagUntilTimeout function

Body:
Hello,

I found that the Timeout parameter in both HAL_I2C_Master_Receive & HAL_I2C_Mem_Read functions is not used in these two lines: 

https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32g0xx_hal_driver/blob/dabe885cefd3c201c1d8aa1cc98657db7b76a309/Src/stm32g0xx_hal_i2c.c#L1273

https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32g0xx_hal_driver/blob/dabe885cefd3c201c1d8aa1cc98657db7b76a309/Src/stm32g0xx_hal_i2c.c#L2670

I'm not sure if this is a bug, but in my case, I need to change it to : 
_if (I2C_WaitOnFlagUntilTimeout(hi2c, I2C_FLAG_BUSY, SET, Timeout, tickstart) != HAL_OK)_

**How to reproduce the "bug "**: Call the HAL_I2C_Master_Receive or HAL_I2C_Mem_Read function with a timeout parameter of less than 25ms, and don't power up the i2c device to trigger the timeout.

Comments:
[KRASTM - 2024-04-26T16:20:23Z]
Hello @Kedrel,

Thank you for the report.

The Timeout used in I2C_WaitOnFlagUntilTimeout for the 2 functions HAL_I2C_Master_Receive & HAL_I2C_Mem_Read is sufficient to check if the peripheral still busy.

Otherwise, can you share more details about your scenario or project?

With regards.

[Kedrel - 2024-04-29T06:48:52Z]
Hello @KRASTM,

The system i'm working on currently uses a tick of 10 ms to run the whole process. The aim is never to have a task that exceends 10ms so we can handle the "real-time" properly.

When i call "**HAL_I2C_Mem_Read**" using a Timeout parameter at 2 ms, inside of it we have the call of "**I2C_WaitOnFlagUntilTimeout**" which uses a parameter of **I2C_TIMEOUT_BUSY**, which is 25ms. 

So if an I2C peripheral can't respond, instead of loosing 2ms of wait time like the setting i chose, i'll loose 25ms. 

I can't afford to loose 25ms like that (as i have multiple I2C sensors), so i'll change the **I2C_TIMEOUT_BUSY** value to something acceptable for my application. 

With regards.

[KRASTM - 2024-04-29T13:31:40Z]
Hello @Kedrel,

In this particular case, it is possible to modify the value of I2C_TIMEOUT_BUSY  to suit your application.
Please allow me to close this issue. Thank you for your comprehension.

With regards.

issue_title: Data filters in LL_ADC_REG_ReadConversionDataX prevent left alignment from working
clean_text:
Title: Data filters in LL_ADC_REG_ReadConversionDataX prevent left alignment from working

Body:
**Describe the set-up**
Any board.
Any IDE/compiler.
Noticed with MC Library with HAL/LL that uses ADC value left alignment.

**Describe the bug**
In recent version of HAL/LL for G0, functions LL_ADC_REG_ReadConversionData12, LL_ADC_REG_ReadConversionData10, LL_ADC_REG_ReadConversionData8 and LL_ADC_REG_ReadConversionData6 were modified with data filters, respectively 0x00000FFFUL, 0x000003FFUL, 0x000000FFUL, and 0x0000003FUL.
This prevent them from working when LL_ADC_DATA_ALIGN_LEFT is configured.

**How To Reproduce**
Any project using MC Library or LL_ADC_DATA_ALIGN_LEFT with G0/HAL_LL.

**Additional context**
Removing the filters mentioned above solves the issue.
For example, for 12 bit data value, the correct function is:

__STATIC_INLINE uint16_t LL_ADC_REG_ReadConversionData12(const ADC_TypeDef *ADCx)
{
  return (uint16_t)(READ_BIT(ADCx->DR, ADC_DR_DATA));
}

Comments:
[RJMSTM - 2023-12-29T14:50:12Z]
ST Internal Reference: 169678

[RJMSTM - 2024-01-05T10:35:04Z]
Hello @phileimer,

This not a bug:
the feature "data alignment" shifts data to be aligned on bit 15, therefore data is 16 bits wide [15; 0].
And therefore, to read data, function LL_ADC_REG_ReadConversionData32() must be used.

The other functions ..._ReadConversionData6/8/10/12 are not usable in this mode.

An update description will be made of LL_ADC_REG_ReadConversionData32() to be more generic on use cases.

With regards,
Rania

Thank you for your feedback. I got the point.
I believe you should fill in a bug for this in the X-CUBE-MCSDK project.

I've not checked with the newer version 6.

Also, I noticed these LL_ADC functions for other STM32 flavors I use (F4 and L0) don't have these data filters implemented yet.
Will they be modified later?

Thank you again,
J. Ph.

[FredericVirot - 2024-04-19T17:21:41Z]

X-CUBE-MCSDK version 6.x also uses a left alignment configuration for the ADCs, so this issue is present in this line of versions. This indeed causes a severe bug as it makes the MCSDK unusable on G0 with the 1.6.2 version of the G0 LL drivers.

issue_title: USB OUT stall's on high bus load
clean_text:
Title: USB OUT stall's on high bus load 

Body:
I have a firmware running on the NUCLEO-G0B1RE that receives bulk out transfers over USB and echos them back.
The endpoint is setup for double buffering.
At high bus load some transfers are aborted with a STALL.

The firmware is ported by @marckleinebudde can be found here https://github.com/marckleinebudde/candleLight_fw/tree/stm32g0

I suspect the cause to be in [Inc/stm32g0xx_ll_usb.h#L659](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32g0xx_hal_driver/blob/master/Inc/stm32g0xx_ll_usb.h#L659).
It does two writes to the buffer descriptor table.
One to clear BLSIZE, NUM_BLOCK and COUNTn_RX and one the set BLSIZE and NUM_BLOCK.
This results in a small window in which NUM_BLOCK is 0 while the endpoint is valid.

As stated in RM0444 37.5.2
> Reception memory buffer locations are written starting from the address contained in the
> ADDRn_RX for a number of bytes corresponding to the received data packet length, or up
> to the last allocated memory location, as defined by BLSIZE and NUM_BLOCK, whichever
> comes first. In this way, the USB peripheral never writes beyond the end of the allocated
> reception memory buffer area. If the length of the data packet payload (actual number of
> bytes used by the application) is greater than the allocated buffer, the USB peripheral
> detects a buffer overrun condition. In this case, a STALL handshake is sent instead of the
> usual ACK to notify the problem to the host, no interrupt is generated and the transaction is
> considered failed.

So either make sure COUNTn_RX is cleared without clearing NUM_BLOCK or setting STATRX to NAK while changing the entry.

Comments:
[ALABSTM - 2024-02-08T18:04:31Z]
Hi @lichtfeind,

Please excuse this delayed reply. Your point looks relevant. It has been forwarded to our development teams for further analysis. I will keep you informed.

To be sure I correctly understood, you suspect the below [code block](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32g0xx_hal_driver/blob/master/Inc/stm32g0xx_ll_usb.h#L683-L704) to cause the issue, mainly the **two successive accesses** to the buffer descriptor table via the pdwReg parameter:
1. to clear both BLSIZE and NBLK,
2. to set them back.

c
#define USB_DRD_SET_CHEP_CNT_RX_REG(pdwReg, wCount) \
  do { \
    uint32_t wNBlocks; \
    \
    (pdwReg) &= ~(USB_CNTRX_BLSIZE | USB_CNTRX_NBLK_MSK); \
    \
    if ((wCount) > 62U) \
    { \
      USB_DRD_CALC_BLK32((pdwReg), (wCount), wNBlocks); \
    } \
    else \
    { \
      if ((wCount) == 0U) \
      { \
        (pdwReg) |= USB_CNTRX_BLSIZE; \
      } \
      else \
      { \
        USB_DRD_CALC_BLK2((pdwReg), (wCount), wNBlocks); \
      } \
    } \
  } while(0) /* USB_DRD_SET_CHEP_CNT_RX_REG */
